description:
The Elliptical Building discovered inside the legionary fortress of Deva Victrix is a unique structure whose unusual form has led to a wide range of interpretations, including a monumental temple connected to the Imperial Cult. Largely uncovered during rescue excavations in the late 1960s, it is a massive 60 x 30m building dressed with high-quality masonry. An internal courtyard contains a central fountain or monument, surrounded by twelve wedge-shaped rooms. These have been interpreted as possible shrines for the twelve major deities of the Roman pantheon (the _Dii Consentes_) or perhaps the twelve signs of the Zodiac.

While the original excavations have been criticised for their poor quality, limiting our knowledge of the site, a lead water pipe was discovered with an inscription dating its manufacture to early 79 CE—only a few years after the fortress was founded. Construction appears to have been quickly abandoned, with the building only completed in the early 3rd century CE in a simplified form. The last known alterations date to around 375 CE, suggesting the building remained in use for some time after this.
